featured_reviews.name: Jubin B
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this place for dinner and tried a few dishes from their Mughlai menu.
We started with the Mutton Turkey Boti, which was recommended by the person taking our order. It was basically mutton kebab coated with red mayo/cream. It was decent, but honestly we were expecting a more authentic Mughlai or Lucknowi Nawab-style flavour. Nowadays adding cream and mayo to everything kind of kills the original richness and taste of such dishes. So for us, this starter didn’t really stand out.

Then we had the Murg Lahori with tandoori roti and butter tandoori roti. This dish was actually very good. The gravy had a rich and authentic flavour. One warning though — if you’re not used to spicy food, this curry can literally make you cry 😄. My wife was continuously drinking water after every bite, but thankfully the taste made up for the spice level.

For dessert, we had the Kaju Katli Ice Cream. This was surprisingly really good. Even though it also had a creamy/malai texture, the flavour worked really well here and it genuinely felt worth the money.
Also, the person who served us was really polite and attentive. The way he was serving felt very warm and caring — almost like how a mother serves food at home, with genuine pyaar se hospitality. That really added to the experience.

Overall, a mixed experience — starter was average for us, but the main course and dessert were enjoyable. Good place if you like rich, spicy Mughlai-style food.

Given that the area has a significant Gujarati community and is largely dominated by vegetarian options, this restaurant provides a refreshing and much-needed alternative for non-vegetarian diners.

The food was well-prepared, flavourful, and lived up to expectations. The biryani and barbeque items were particularly enjoyable, with balanced spices and good portion sizes. The service was prompt and courteous, contributing positively to the overall experience.

Overall, it is a dependable choice for those looking for good non-vegetarian options in Borivali West, and I would certainly recommend it for a satisfying meal.

This is a restaurant 🏨 chain ⛓️ in Mumbai, known for its Mughlai 🍢 and non-veg food. I won't recommend this place much if you are Jain 👳or pure vegetarian 🥬. It's a 2 florey restaurant with AC 🌬️ and Non-AC 🪭 section usually the restaurant is packed during weekend. The name of the restaurant is BBC (Borivali Biryani 🍚 Center) known for its Biryani and majorly non-veg. If talking about the staff 🧑‍💼 they were occupied a lot and a bit ignorant about the customer 🙂, I asked 3-4 times for the same thing to different people still could not get much respond. The ambience ✨ of of Family restaurant and cleanliness 🧹 is maintained. Washroom is unisex and 🫧 clean however there was water blocked at some place.

Further, talking about the foods and the drinks that we tried :

1. Blue bliss - it's basically a lemonade 🍋 with an added food colour 🔵, it was sweet but an good option from the mocktail menu.

2. Virgin mojito 🍸- Just an old school taste of soda 🥤mixed with lemon 🧃 juice and with some basil 🌿 leafs in it.

3. Lemon Iced Tea ☕- It's a cool starter in drinks 🍷 to go with along with some heavy food.

3. Veg dum biryani 🌾- It's a simple option if you don't want to explore kuch and it's a safer option. I asked them to make it a bit spicy 🔥. A taste of mixed vegetables 🍆 and paneer served with boondi raita.

4. Paneer Crispy Plum  - It's a chinese sweet🍯 starter with some added veggies. I usually don't prefer sweets so I won't recommend the same.

5. Mushroom  🍄 Tikka - It's just like paneer tikka 🍢 but instead paneer mushroom 🍄 is used. For a change you can try mushrooms instead of Paneer.

The overall experience was okay as the staff was not attentive, the food taste in veg was not that good and I didn't have much to explore on the menu. You can go here for mughlai and kebabs dish 🍽️.

They also serve good Chinese and Continental options. The Manchow Soup, Hakka Noodles, and Crispy Veg are quite popular among regulars.

The ambience is elegant and comfortable — dim lighting, spacious seating, and a relaxed family-friendly vibe. It’s clean, well-maintained, and gives a premium dining feel without being overly expensive.

Banjara Restaurant in Borivali is a perfect blend of taste, comfort, and quality. Whether you’re dining with family, celebrating a special occasion, or simply craving rich Indian food, this place never disappoints. Highly recommended for food lovers who value both flavor and atmosphere.

Biryani by Kilo

Biryani by Kilo is the hub of delicious Biryanis in Mumbai with 3 outlets. They have varieties in Biryani. They also have Kebabs, Kormas and Curries with Indian Breads.

As the name suggests they serve Biryani 1 Kg and ½ Kg in sealed earthen clay pot. They expertise in all types of Biryanis, be it Hyderabadi, Lucknowi or Kolkata Biryani. It is not only the biryani was nice with perfect flavors but also the entire experience of heating the Biryani with a small candle that comes along when you are unpacking the pot gives you a more satisfaction. Amazing!!!

Recently I have ordered the food from Andheri East outlet. The food delivery received on time and the food was warm with proper packaging.

What I tried:

Mutton Galouti Kebab: It was juicy, very soft and tender. The chutney comes along with was nice. Perfect in taste and texture was nice. Do try.

Chicken Korma: It was so tasty to be honest. Served in small clay pot. Enough for 2 people. The brown gravy was thick and perfect. A must recommended for Non vegetarian lovers.

Chicken Hyderbadi Biryani: Delicious Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani loaded with spicy marinated chicken, onions and flavorful saffron rice. Very happy to see Biryani was not at oily and hot. Perfect blend of long grain rice, spices and chicken pieces. Good to go to try this one.

Phirni: Not too sweet and consistency was thick. Good to go.

Overall, the food was fresh and piping hot with a good aroma. The quantity was adequate considering the pricing.

In my opinion you can check out this outlet for an Instant delivery of Biryani and Kebabs as well.

Food: 5/5

Delivery: 5/5

Packaging: 5/5

P.S: The review is strictly depending on my personal experience.

I visited today at 1:50 pm. There were people in waiting outside.

featured_reviews.name: Ajay Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited The Bliss Cuisine and Libation on 26th May 2026 to celebrate my parents' anniversary, expecting a pleasant fine-dining experience. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of the most disappointing restaurant visits I've had.

We ordered Soup, Prawns Tempura Sushi (4 pcs), and Chicken Chilly. The soup was decent, but the problems started when the sushi arrived. The portion size was surprisingly small compared to what is typically served at good restaurants. While I was willing to overlook that, the bigger issue was the filling. There was hardly any prawn in the sushi—most of what we got was the fried coating. To make matters worse, the dish contained minced prawn instead of actual prawn pieces, which was not what we expected.

When I politely raised this concern with the waiter, his response was rude and dismissive. He simply said, "This is how we make it here," in a tone that was far from customer-friendly. This is not how paying customers should be spoken to, especially in a restaurant that positions itself as a fine-dining establishment.

I requested to speak with the manager. While the manager listened to the issue, no effort was made to resolve it. I asked them to take the dish back and remove it from the bill, but they refused. I even offered to pay half the price of the dish as a compromise, but there was no flexibility. I then requested them to cancel our pending order and bring the bill.

What made the experience worse was that despite repeated apologies from Manager , there was no acknowledgment from the waiter regarding his behavior. The lack of accountability and basic courtesy completely spoiled what was supposed to be a special family occasion.

We paid the bill and left feeling disrespected rather than valued as customers.

If you're looking for good hospitality and customer service, I would recommend looking elsewhere. The food may be average, but poor service and disrespectful behavior are far harder to overlook.

I hope the owner takes customer feedback seriously and trains the staff on how to interact professionally with patrons. Experiences like this can drive customers away and damage the restaurant's reputation.

featured_reviews.name: Rajesh Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
much of the persian and mughlai cooking has it roots in the way soldiers were fed. fighting wars far away from home often meant fresh ingredients found in abundance at home didnt survive the long campaigns.. however what did travel well were the dry spices. so the cooks wove the spices into all that they cooked. the thing with spices it that not all spices mix with eachother and the proportions have to be meticulously followed. striking the right balance is key and the khamsamas at Persian Durbar are fanatic about it. lets take the Barra Kababs, they are often thought to be a spicy dish and made as such, with focus on hot spices and chillies, but do taste them here to understand that barra is more about the tenderness and subtle spices and slow roasting. the best i ever sampled

this attention to detail is seen in pretty much every dish, what needs to be spicy is spicy, nihari, for instance, what needs to be mild is mild, botis for example and what needs to be tender yet juicy, is just that with no hint of dryness, the raans...

take your time, savour slowly, the persians took their time at meals, so should you

We loved the food — the white sauce pasta was creamy and delicious, the dry Manchurian was flavourful, and the mint paneer was equally delicious. We also tried their special Belgium Brownie milkshake, which was super chocolaty and absolutely indulgent.

If you’re a fan of authentic, well-made kulchas, Sai Kripa does not disappoint. Their kulchas are:

✅ Perfectly Crisp & Fluffy – The outer layer has a satisfying crispiness, while the inside remains soft and slightly chewy.

✅ Well-Stuffed & Flavorful – Whether it’s aloo, paneer, or mixed stuffing, they don’t skimp on ingredients. The masala is balanced, with a slight tang and spice kick that complements the kulcha beautifully.

✅ Served with the Right Pairings – A good kulcha is incomplete without chole, raita, or chutney, and Sai Kripa gets this right. Their chole is rich and well-spiced, making for a fulfilling combination.

✅ Good Portion & Value for Money – Generous portions at reasonable pricing make it a great choice for a hearty meal.

Overall, if you’re looking for a place that nails a classic North Indian-style kulcha, Sai Kripa is worth a visit.

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
